title: Tata Electronics Signs Five Semiconductor Partnerships in a Single Day
excerpt: The Tata Electronics agreements — with Nexperia, Fujifilm, Besi, SCL and a skilling university — span chip fabrication, materials, advanced packaging and talent as India pushed to build a complete semiconductor ecosystem at SEMICON India 2026.
body:
• Tata Electronics announced five partnerships in a single day on September 17, 2026, spanning chip fabrication, materials, advanced packaging, indigenization and talent.
  • The headline deal with Dutch chipmaker Nexperia covers wafer fabrication at the Dholera Fab and assembly and test at the Jagiroad facility in Assam.
  • Fujifilm committed roughly INR 800 crore to localize semiconductor materials near Dholera; Besi brings advanced packaging equipment to Jagiroad.
  • The two flagship builds carry a combined investment of USD 14 billion as SEMICON India 2026 opened with Rs 1 lakh crore in commitments.

Five deals in a single day

Tata Electronics unveiled five partnerships in one day on September 17, 2026, each aimed at a different gap in India's emerging semiconductor ecosystem. The announcements came on Day 1 of SEMICON India 2026, inaugurated by the Prime Minister in New Delhi for its fifth edition, where the government reported Rs 1 lakh crore in investment commitments and 16 MoUs and announcements across the chip value chain.

The headline agreement was a strategic partnership with Nexperia, the Dutch semiconductor major with more than 12,500 employees and over 100 billion products shipped annually. Structured around three areas — front-end wafer fabrication, back-end assembly and test, and technology and ecosystem development — the framework lays the groundwork to produce Nexperia's MOSFET portfolio at Tata Electronics' upcoming 300mm fab in Dholera, Gujarat, while Nexperia's discrete semiconductor products will be assembled and tested at Tata's packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam.

"We are thrilled to partner with Nexperia for manufacturing their products at our semiconductor facilities in Dholera and Jagiroad."

— Dr. Randhir Thakur, CEO & Managing Director, Tata Electronics

Thakur added that the collaboration aligns with the growing technology and trade relationship between India and the European Union. Nexperia's interim CEO Stefan Tilger said the partnership brings together "complementary strengths across technology, manufacturing and innovation" while reinforcing a "resilient and globally balanced manufacturing network," and its COO Achim Kempe described it as "much more than manufacturing."

Materials, packaging, indigenization, talent

Japan's FUJIFILM Corporation signed an MoU to accelerate the semiconductor materials ecosystem around the Dholera fab, becoming one of the first movers to localize critical raw materials in the region. Fujifilm will invest roughly INR 800 crore (about US$83 million) in phases to set up a semiconductor materials plant in the Dholera Special Investment Region, and will support Indian chemical manufacturers with technology, quality assurance and process know-how to produce high-purity chemicals.

Fujifilm CEO Teiichi Goto called India's expanding market "a critical opportunity." The Dholera fab itself, being built at a total investment of INR 91,000 crore (about US$11 billion), will produce chips across 28nm to 110nm nodes for automotive, consumer electronics, computing, wireless and AI applications.

Dutch assembly-equipment leader Besi signed an MoU to strengthen advanced packaging capabilities at the US$3 billion Jagiroad facility, supplying its portfolio of die-attach, flip-chip, thermo-compression and hybrid bonding technologies. The deal builds on the India-Netherlands MoU on semiconductors and emerging technologies. Besi CEO and Chairman Richard Blickman called it "a shared commitment to innovation, technology development and the advancement of the semiconductor industry," while Thakur noted that advanced packaging is "rapidly becoming one of the most critical differentiators in semiconductor innovation."

Tata Electronics also partnered with the Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL) — India's only Integrated Device Manufacturing facility, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology — to advance semiconductor indigenization across design, process technology, supply-chain localization and talent. The collaboration targets chip design for government and startup projects and priorities in aerospace, defence and strategic domains, building on the government's "Make in India, Innovate with India, Scale for the World" call. SCL Director General Dr. Kanwaljeet Singh said the partnership blends SCL's end-to-end capabilities with Tata's foundry, OSAT infrastructure and global customer reach.

The final agreement, with Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, a central university focused on transport, infrastructure and logistics, creates a talent pipeline for chip manufacturing. The multi-party framework, which also includes L&T EduTech and Jacobs Solutions, will develop curriculum, joint certifications and skilling programs in semiconductor facility engineering, project management, and logistics and supply chain. Thakur noted that semiconductor fabs are "among the most sophisticated industrial facilities in the world," making domestic talent development essential as India builds an ecosystem of global standards.

Building an ecosystem, not just plants

The strategy on display is to assemble an integrated, end-to-end semiconductor base in India rather than a single plant: the two flagship builds — India's first commercial semiconductor fab in Dholera and the country's first indigenous assembly and test facility in Jagiroad — represent a combined investment of USD 14 billion, anchored by global manufacturing partners (Nexperia), materials supply (Fujifilm), packaging technology (Besi), strategic indigenization (SCL) and a homegrown workforce.

Thakur said Tata Electronics would sign 16 agreements at SEMICON India across Europe, Japan, Singapore and India — with Nexperia and Besi from Europe; JSR, Fujifilm, Sumitomo, Sojitz and Ajinomoto from Japan; Kelington from Malaysia; Ascendas and First Space from Singapore; and domestic players such as L&T Semiconductors, Inox Air Products, SCL and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya. Those follow an earlier partnership with lithography equipment provider ASML, and a separate MoU with Ascendas First Space to develop a 363-acre vendor park in Dholera.

He told the conference that both greenfield sites remain on track to meet commitments made to the government, with more than 450 ecosystem partners engaged at Dholera across construction, chemicals, equipment and materials. "Five years ago, the India Semiconductor Mission was formed. Today, there are 12 factories in different stages of completion, and we are already exporting Made in India chips to customers globally," Thakur said. He also said Tata Electronics has created over 1,50,000 direct jobs, that each semiconductor job creates 10 jobs in the ecosystem, that 65 percent of its workforce are women, and that 300 recent Indian university graduates are undergoing technical training at partner PSMC's fabrication facilities in Taiwan.

Diaspora Angle

The ecosystem push resonates with the Indian diaspora's deep bench in the global semiconductor industry, where Indian-origin engineers hold senior roles across major chip firms in the US, Taiwan and Europe — a talent pool Tata Electronics will need to complement as it stands up homegrown fabs, and one that already follows India's chip ambitions closely.

What's Next

SEMICON India 2026 runs through September 19, with further MoUs and announcements expected across the value chain. Beyond Tata's builds, the government flagged one lakh technicians to be trained over five years, six ChipIN Regional Centres to widen chip-design access, and continued progress at facilities such as Micron's commercial DRAM and NAND production at Sanand — signals that the next test of the ecosystem will be moving from signed agreements to operating fabs.
